messages:
maria.garcia: Heads up — brought up a new embed candidate 'silhouette-v2' on staging. Quick smoke: recall@1/5/10 looked okay but silhouette score dropped vs baseline.
josh.kim: ok can you paste the numbers? roughs are fine
maria.garcia: recall@1 0.62 -> baseline 0.64, recall@10 0.83 -> 0.85. Silhouette mean: 0.39 vs baseline 0.51. cluster sizes a bit imbalanced.
anna: that silhouette drop is kinda big. is it across all languages or just en?
maria.garcia: mostly EN and DE. Multilang holdouts looked flat. I ran UMAP+HDBSCAN, clusters are more diffuse.
liam: were you running quantized weights or fp16? which artifact?
maria.garcia: fp16 checkpoint from model hub. Also ran int8 PTQ quick sweep: int8 recall@10 drops to 0.78, silhouette 0.34. So quant hurts more than fp16.
josh.kim: thanks. did you run the standard anchor-holdout set? any change in nearest neighbor distances?
maria.garcia: yes anchor set. median cosine neighbor delta +0.015 vs baseline (i.e., embeddings slightly closer). But variance increased, more long-tail neighbors.
anna: maybe the embedding norm distribution shifted. Can you share norm hist?
maria.garcia: pasted plot to thread (image). quick stats: mean norm 1.02 -> baseline 0.98, std 0.22 -> 0.13.
liam: that matches the diffuse clusters. higher mean and higher spread.
ops-bot: deploy:staging finished for artifact silhouette-v2@2026-03-20T18:45:12Z :white_check_mark:
josh.kim: can you run a bias/cluster-size table? kmeans(k=50) cluster counts, top 5 cluster sizes vs baseline
maria.garcia: short table:
- silhouette-v2 top5 cluster sizes: [1124, 980, 440, 330, 301]
- baseline top5: [980, 870, 540, 420, 320]
so silhouette has a couple of larger hubs.
anna: hubs could explain recall changes — more examples collapsing into a few dense clusters, pushing others away.
maria.garcia: agree. hypothesis: training objective tweak increased local attraction for frequent tokens/context.
liam: action items?
josh.kim: 1) rerun with L2 normalization postfix (embedding /= ||e||) to see if norm shift is driver
2) run calibrated int8 (per-channel) instead of PTQ to check quant degradation
3) run recall stratified by freq bins (top1k vs tail)
maria.garcia: doing (1) now. quick note: I tested L2 normalize on a 10k sample, recall@10 recovered to 0.84, silhouette 0.47 — big improvement.
anna: nice. that points to norm issue rather than semantic capacity.
liam: for int8 try this command on the quantizer box:
```
quantize --model silhouette-v2 --mode perchannel --calib-samples 20000 --out artifact-int8-perc
```
liam: that should help preserve recall.
josh.kim: also add the eval for recall@k on the short-query holdout (we saw regressions there historically)
maria.garcia: queued short-query run, will share logs. prelim short-query recall@1 dropped from 0.58 -> 0.49 on fp16, but with L2 norm it's 0.57.
anna: ok so normalization is necessary in the serving stack as a safety. we should add it to rollout gating.
maria.garcia: proposal: add an automatic norm-check step in onboarding: check mean/std and run L2-normalize probe; flag if delta > 0.05 or silhouette delta > 0.05.
josh.kim: +1. also add per-channel quant check and require recall@10 within -0.02 of baseline on anchor set before allowing int8 default.
liam: I'll add a Jenkins job to run the quant per-channel calibration and short-query stratified recall. tagging @eng-infra to give it resources.
maria.garcia: logs and full numbers: will drop artifact + eval json here when done. for now, marking this as "needs-normalization".
anna: TY. good catch; glad smoke caught it before rollout.
maria.garcia: thanks everyone. will update with final int8 artifacts and numbers.
ops-bot: ticket #ENGML-1428 created for "silhouette-v2 onboarding: normalization + quant checks"
